institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Of course all the above mentioned aspects were important to my decision, whilst the opportunity to explore new cultures was the most important. Denmark and Norway are similar in many aspects, but in Northern Norway nature and outdoor life e.g skiing plays a big role in the everyday life, which i really wanted to experience. Furthermore, Norway is not an unlikely work destination for danish doctors.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been nice with an introduction to the other exchange students and being a bit more included at the university instead of just being at the hospital.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Much information were given on the first day of clinical rotation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When and where to meet the first day of clinical rotation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again, further introduction at the university would have been nice

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy through Samskipnaden.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is best to live on the Island of Tromsø. The university is located a couple of kilometers away from city centre, but it is very easy to go to the university by bus. Would recommend to find housing with local norwegians.

questions.answer: A bit messy. Much writing back and forth with a bit of divergent information. Might be due to staff being on sick leave.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guides and the international coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have any courses, only clinical rotation.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to fill out the registration papers as good as you can and send it to the international coordinators. They will let you know, if anything is missing.

questions.answer: Vegetables, alcohol and meat are very expensive, but i knew this in advance.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, parties, museum tours etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try some of the bars, go hiking, skiing, stay overnight at a "hytte", go on a roadtrip to e.g. Senja or Lofoten.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The above mentioned.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, due to Denmark and Norway being much alike.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to speak norwegian, find housing with local norwegians, embrace the outdoor life.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Actually i would say the same as above "Try to speak norwegian, find housing with local norwegians, embrace the outdoor life." In addition, a car is very useful to have and Norway is very expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: To summarize: Find housing through Samskipnaden, live with norwegians, embrace outdoor life, buy skis, be aware that Norway is very expensive, get a car if possible, go on roadtrips.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The outdoor life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to reach everything, whilst having mandatory full time clinical rotation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
